items.title: UI drive (agent controls the app)
items.summary: An agent can now open Settings, switch sections, open a canvas, doc, issue or chat, open a web page, point at a control or show a note, all on your screen. Every screen change shows a Deny button first and an Undo button after.

features.name: Open something, with Deny and Undo
features.what: Before: an agent could only reply in text, it could not move you around the app. Now: when the agent writes a command line (for example `@tempo-ui open settings`) or runs the CLI, the app opens Settings by itself. A small toast shows Deny while it moves, then Undo to go back.
features.how: Nothing to do. Click Deny to stop it, Undo to go back, or Always allow to stop seeing the toast.

media.caption: Agent writes a command, Settings opens, the toast offers Undo (fixture)
Toast with a Deny button while the command runs (fixture)
After it ran: Undo and Always allow (fixture)

features.name: Deny a command
features.what: Before: no way to stop an agent. Now: pressing Deny while the beam flies cancels the move and nothing changes on screen.

media.caption: Agent asks to go to the canvas, user clicks Deny, the app stays where it was (fixture)

features.name: Point at a control and show a note
features.what: Before: an agent could only describe a button in words. Now: it can scroll to a control and highlight it, or show a short note toast.
features.how: Automatic, from the agent (focus and toast commands).

media.caption: Agent highlights a card, then shows a note toast (fixture)

features.name: Safety rules
features.what: Before: not applicable. Now: only a fixed list of commands runs. Code (eval), bad links (javascript:, file:) and unknown actions are refused with a short toast. Risky actions, like deleting, run only after you click Allow, and are never always-allowed.
features.how: Click Allow in the toast for a risky action. Otherwise it expires after 10 seconds.

media.caption: A destructive action asks for an explicit Allow (fixture)

features.video: n/a: covered by the stills, the clips above show the same toast

items.title: UI beam (agent handoff animation)
items.summary: When an agent uses the UI, you now see it: a pulse on the message, a beam with the Claude avatar flying to the control, then a frame around the target.

features.name: Message to target flight
features.what: Before: things just changed on screen with no clue why. Now: a pulse starts at the agent message, a rounded beam with the Claude avatar flies to the target (about 1 second), and a frame fades in around it.
features.how: Automatic when ui-drive runs a command.

media.caption: Beam flying from a chat message to a button (fixture)

features.name: Target frame and reduced motion
features.what: Before: not applicable. Now: the target keeps a soft rounded frame for about 1.5 seconds. With reduced motion on, there is no travel, only a short pulse and the frame. It can be turned off in localStorage (rtd.uiBeam = off).

media.caption: Reduced motion: pulse and frame only (fixture)

features.video: n/a: the flight clip above already shows the frame

items.title: App map (named controls for agents)
items.summary: A live list of every button, field and toggle on screen, each with a stable readable name, plus the app's actions. Agents can find and use a control by name instead of guessing pixels.

features.name: Stable names and debug overlay
features.what: Before: an agent saw only pixels. Now: every clickable or typeable control gets a name such as `rail/button/settings` and a risk color (green safe, orange caution, red destructive). A debug overlay draws all names on screen.
features.how: For developers: run `__RE_TEMPO_APP_MAP__.debug(true)` in the console.

media.caption: Overlay turned on, then a search, then a click by name (fixture)
Every control labeled with its id and colored by risk (fixture)

features.name: Find and click by name
features.what: Before: not possible. Now: an agent can ask for `split right` and get the matching controls, then click, type, toggle, select or drag them by id. Destructive controls are refused unless confirmed.
features.how: Agent commands such as `tempo-ui ui.find split right` and `tempo-ui ui.click <id>`.

media.caption: Search result for 'split right' with risk labels (fixture)

items.title: tempo-ui command line
items.summary: A small command an agent runs in the terminal to drive the open Tempo window (open settings, open a canvas, take a screenshot...). The window answers and the result prints back.

features.name: Help and agent instructions
features.what: Before: Tempo's agent had no way to touch the app UI. Now: it runs `tempo-ui open settings` and the window does it with the beam and Deny/Undo. `tempo-ui --instructions` prints a text to paste into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md so any agent knows the commands.
features.video: n/a: plain text output, the command channel is shown in the ui-drive clips
